This is a game about hacking other computers for a cause, or for fun.
Having been a long time player of Uplink and then Street Hacker I was really hoping that this would provide the drama of Uplink with the technicality of Street Hacker.

Hacknet pulls it off brilliantly!
Excellent game.  Would be amazing to see it go multiplayer somehow, perhaps have more scope to write own .exe files in the game as well.  However - Hacknet is great.

[h1]What to expect if you're new to this game genre[/h1]
Hacknet is a new title in the otherwise stagnant, indie genre of hacking simulation games.
And a fresh breeze it is.

No doubt there is hardly any competition for this kind of quality.
Graphics are amazing, the hacking system introduced is quite good and consistent, it has gigantic potential for expansion that desperately needs to be used, and hopefully will. In it's current shape there might be little room for multiplayer gameplay, because of the game mechanics, but hopefully as the game gets finalized it will be implemented.

The puzzles you have to face are fun to solve and most of the time at medium or easy difficulty level.
Even though the game description provided on Steam might be a little misleading, as to non-holywood hacking style, or minimal hand-holding, the gameplay can be extremely exciting and satisfying.
The thrill of hacking, taking unauthorised control over websites, other web services, or user machines and mobile devices, identity theft or destruction, and constantly racing the trace clock are all very satisfying and will give you an addictive adrenaline rush.

Music is a very proper and enjoyable background for your virtual crimes, not quite something to remember.

The game has too high hardware requirements in my opinion. All in all it is a console based hacking game, and it is barely playable on i5, 4GB, Intel graphics HD4000 Lenovo laptop (12 fps max with too much typing lag!!!)

[h1]Finally the 'Uplink vs Hacknet'[/h1]
Many people look up to Hacknet in comparison to Uplink.
Based on my experiences with both titles If you did truly enjoy Uplink, You will be dazzled by Hacknet's modern design. Graphics are eyecandy.
The gameplay itself however, as compared to Uplink I have found to be short (if that can be said - I was unable to finish the game due to numerous bugs [despite 50+hrs in-game]), shallow and at many times unchallenging.
If you can bear with, well kinda outdated graphics and a little clumsy UI, I'd say Uplink offers far greater immersion, much more complex world to explore, more freedom, less hand holding.
Hardware upgrades covering several computer components to your machine, or even different, more upgradable machines (you can create them yourself or download one of many community created ones!!!!), software upgrades that all can be purchased are something you won't find in Hacknet, since finances have been taken out of the picture in the first place. Money earning, stock market participation and manipulation, and banking are all absent in Hacknet. So are LAN networks that pose a sublevel of gameplay in Uplink. Hacknet at this stage of developement also gives you the feeling of being the only web user out there, since only on rare story related events will you ever find logs left by anyone else on any servers (even the public services). Tracing other hackers or users is nearly non existent since the idea of connection bouncing has also been skipped so far. In my opinion, with similar development times of several years for both games, Uplink is a masterpiece bot technically and story-wise, compared to Hacknet.

[h1]Final words[/h1]
Whatever Hacknet is or will be, I'd say Uplink is worth playing, as the only other hacking game out there with some serious gameplay to this date.
If compatibility issues or the kinda-outdated-look are an obstacle for you playing Uplink, Hacknet will still be a very enjoyable and exciting experience, however I would strongly advise to wait with the purchase until numerous major bugs are addressed and more potential gets released from Hacknet, or you might be facing quite a frustrating struggle with what I can only call a beta version (at best) right now. I have also learned there is a free remake of Uplink to be found out there, I will let you find it yourself tho, since I'd stick with the original version by Introversion Software and support it's makers.
Keep track of Hacknet news and discussion on Steam for a stable version somewhen in the (hopefully) near future.

reviews.review: A very interesting game that is engaging and fun. It doesn't hold your hand all that much leaving you to actually figure things out for yourself and find your own stlye of sorts. Fantastic story thus far! I hope to see more of this game in the future.

This game is absolute blast to play. While, a bit more on the shorter side, the story and gameplay are filled up with tons of interesting things that will keep you immersed and continously playing all the way up to the end. 

The game itself consists of just you in a terminal layout and going around hacking websites and finding out what happened to the character "Bit" as there is more to what actually happened to him then meets the eye. Even if you aren't a hacker wizard (like myself), this game is really easy on guiding you in with tons of tutorials and hints and having easy buttons like TAB to fill out the programs and make it a bit more friendly to the average player. 

The story is really really immersive and honestly along with the soundtrack is the best thing about the game. The creators really did a great job of making you feel like you are the actual hacker and you are the one that is under the control of all of this. Moving around and seeing all the ways the story builds up is suspenseful, well done, and overall kept me really going and a bit suspenseful at times. The soundtrack is also top notch by the way, which help to not only add to the immersion but really help tense up at suspenseful parts in the game and also really melodic when it needs to which is also a huge plus.

In the end, Hacknet is a brilliant hacking game with puzzle/mystery solving elements, a beautiful soundtrack, a wonderful story, and in overall a great game. I don't expect this to be for everyone because the terminal layout is all you're going to see and this game does a real job portraying you as a hacker so it can be a bit tricky at times, but in the end, it's something that I believe that you should try out if you're willing to tackle on the puzzles and mysteries, as this is definitely  not a game for just the casual puzzle solver.

All in all, fantastic game albeit a bit short and sometimes a bit tricky and difficult.

reviews.review:
It's an ok hacking game, with somewhat of a focus on "realism".
The storyline is fine, but the depth of the game mechanics themselves (tracing, tools, mission system, communication system, the "internet" itself) leaves a lot to be desired.
Still not a worthy sucessor to uplink, with nowhere near as depth in the world or gameplay itself. But I guess that's all we have now that the Onlink project is as good as dead.
The soundtrack, however, is AMAZING. I'd go as far as saying that it's the best part of the game.

If you are a fan of the hacking games that have been popping up now and then over the years, well; this may be the one that you have been waiting for. It truly takes all of the best aspects of the myriad hacker games already around. It expands on them and gives them some finesse tweaks. Some of the hacking games out there were too limited, too small, too difficult, too unforgiving and just too FAIL. That is just my take on a lot of the games in this genre. Not to say that they are all bad, but they all have a plethora of plusses and minuses. When these balance out, it does NOT make for a good game. The plusses need to far outweigh the minuses if they want to go all in for the win. Well, HACKNET is the closest competitor as far as I am concerned. I am very glad I bought this game and have thoroughly enjoyed my time so far.

Now if you are looking for some cinewmatic story telling cyberpunk 3d rendered world of the hacker, then keep on looking. Aside from some menu effects and wallpapers on your virtual terminal, you will not be seeing much in the video area. Instead this is a simulation of old school hacking... Just a boy and his terminal... A lot of typing... Although the game has a trick for saving your fingers a bit. Most commands and paramters of the commands (once you know what they are) just need the first letter or two or maybe four. Hit the TAB key and the terminal will finish the command for you. If there are parameters or variables to be entered as well, thenh you can TAB through those as well.

Now, I am an old school computer user from back in the day. I mean, when I went online for thye first time I had to dial a phone number by hand and then listen for a computer to answer (screeching carrier signal) then very quickly unplug the phone line and plug it into my modem, Then jump into a terminal program and start typing AT commands to make it answer the phone HOPEFULLY. ANYWAYS, I am old school I have done my timeshare on a dumb terminal application.

I paid my dues with a few ring-backs, shoes and FCC triangulating vans of doom. Had a lot of fun with some phreaking, blue boxes and endless hours dialing into Telnet without ever knowing back then that we were the first surfers to hit the oncoming waves of an approaching storm called the internet. What is my point? I am familiar with doing everything from a CLI and "trading" apps, docs and other information that could be used to further our online escapades. This game SORT OF brings back memories of a bygone era.

Hacknet is one of the best hacking simulators I have ever seen. not only does it look realistic, but it uses legitamate UNIX commands in the game. anyone familiar with linux will enjoy this, but if you don't, who cares?! let me tell you what this game has to offer.

first of all, it has a reasonably interesting plotline. I won't say much, but lets put it this way. Bit is a deceased hacker, and you have to find out how he REALLY died. through missions, you get closer to finding the truth, and getting the justice he deserves.
Depending on how you play, you end up following different paths. one being the Entropy path, the other being CSEC, and one more that I'll let you figure out on your own ;)
The GUI of the game is simple and beutiful. it lays everything out in an organized manner that puts all the control in your hands. Not only that, but the audio is just as good as the visuals. The music in this game is something that gets you pumped up for what's coming your way. and if you're into techno, great. I mean, what did you expect from a hacking/computer-based game? opera? pop? not a chance.
One thing I will say though, this game can get REALLY frustrating, and I'm not putting that lightly. You will have to use your brain to get through this game. regardless, the mechanics are simplistic and easy to learn, but the missions aren't exactly what I would call "a walk in the park".

Finally, in the words of the game's creator himself, Matt Trobbiani, "I do kind of hope I'm creating the Hackers of the future, and I think that's great."
Best hacking game since Uplink! Scared the daylights out of me when it got BSOD. Very realistic! Actually uses real commands instead of made up stuff.

This game is honestly one of the best games I have played. Hacknet is a hacking simulator which may or may not be realistic, I am not a hacker or very good with computers so I would not know but without a doubt it's worth every penny of those $10.00. The game focuses on you as the main character who is suddenly emailed by a enigmatic hacker by the name of bit who teaches you his techniques which launchs off your career as a hacker. As the game goes on you will later be approached by more and more hackers and hacker organizations. One thing I find so enjoyable is the problem solving aspect, sure plenty of the game is just using the tools at your disposal to get into this system or to hack that site but at times your knowledge of the system and the games mechanics will be put to the test. If you have any chance of beating this game you need to be smart, creative, quick to react, and you cannot break under pressure because this game can get pretty intense. Another great aspect of this game it the difficulty. At first it's relatively easy but as time goes on you will begin to notice how this game is unforgiving when you screw up. Not kidding, it's brutal here dude. The game will have multiple instances where a rival hacker is at your throat or when you have a trace running on you and you need to open and hack the ports as fast as possible to become an admin and stop the trace. Sometimes it's going to look bleak but it is soooooo satisfying when you hack the system with seconds to spare and sooooo disapointing when you fail and are wacked over the nose as a result. That does not mean this game is without problems. For one even though the format of the game is its greatest strength it also can be its greatest weakness mainly due to the fact that it is not a very engaging experience and requires you to try your best to stay on top of actually playing the game. The narrative is good without a doubt but it also can get dull at times and even kind of confusing. It's more of a mystery of trying to figure out what happened to Bit but it seems as if they tried to squeez in more and though for the most part the game flows beautifully at times it does get a little cramped. I also have a personal complaint, every time I start the game, even though my profile is still their, it starts me off at the beggining. I don't know if this is supposed to happen or not but I would assume not. I continue trying to find a solution but otherwise I have to beat the game in one consistan run which is kind of erritating but still fun. overally solid 8.5/10, worth buying.

This is an OK game. I wouldn't go as far as to compare it to either Uplink or the Street Hacker series simply because it feels more like a demo when compared to them. The execution and gameplay is shallow and naive. It's plagued by many basic design issues and most of the missions are just boring, repetitive, and feel more like a chore rather than a challenge.

My biggest gripes are:
-boring, repetitive and easy missions. Only 2 interesting missions stand out, the final Bit one, and the online pacemaker one.
-no sense of urgency or challenge. If you get caught hacking, that's just a reload to last checkpoint. No point in deleting any logs the way Uplink makes sure that you do. Uplink kept you on your toes because getting caught meant absolute game over!
-Badly designed UI. The workstation "map" is a cluttered mess especially as you move closer towards the end. Nodes are being randomly generated and the ones closest to the edge of the screen have their hover information cut off. How that ever went past the testers, I do not know!
-Weird writing, bad grammar, spelling mistakes, juvenile jokes scattered here and there. The ending was incredibly cheesy and anti-climactic.

Not a bad game to get on sale. But this is no Uplink for sure. The tagline shouldn't be "if you liked Uplink, you'll love this!" It's more the other way around because now I definitely feel like going back and replaying Uplink for the zillionth time! :)

The successor to legendary hacking game Uplink is finally here. It takes one legend to take over another.

Improvements over Uplink (sorry there is no other game good enough to compare this with):

+ It actually involves less clicking than Uplink, and instead more typing. You type commands to the console to do shit.
+ You can change the color of your interface to your liking. (which was static blue in Uplink)
+ Way many more mission types than Uplink
+ Hacking concept is up to date, not that of 90s
+ More active storyline than Uplink

+ Sometimes the game surprises you out of the fuckin' blue

Note that I loved Uplink, played it for many hours until my eyes started tearing up, still play it from time to time, and have never considered a hacking game come close to its beauty and/or fun level. I was in highschool when Uplink was around, and after like 10 years finally a game comes to take the throne. This game is an all round improvement to Uplink's best features. These are all my humble opinion.

Note, this is more like a linux-based command typing game and still includes a little Hollywood style hacking (because of some hacking sequences' visualizations). If you are not into typing stuff (though most of the time, you can still choose to click instead) or you don't like staring at a screen full of little lines full of console commands, then this game might not be for you. But this was a long expected hacking game, and you can tell that the developer worked his/her ass off while trying to build this.

Hits a really good balance between the tedious busywork of Uplink and the clickety-click oversimplification of Hacker Evolution Duality. While this game doesn't depict hacking realistically, it does present a series of pretty entertaining puzzles and tons of not only flavor text, but also side activities with a few nuggets of cool hidden content. It may sound stupid, but it reminded me of that really gimmicky and ultimately pretty useless Enter the Matrix minigame (that I *loved*), only properly turned into a 10 hour game. It also adds the ability for the player to alter files and it allows him/her to "communicate" with the rest of NPCs (not really, the game just expects sometimes to say something but most of the time is just flavor. I still found it fun and immersive to use, even if it's ultimately pointless most times.)

The story becomes a bit too rushed towards the very ending, which is a bit of a shame, but overall at 1€ per hour -and I gotta admit I kinda nolifed it a bit- is a pretty great value for a game that not only is wildly entertaining and surprisingly tense at times, it will feel super confortable if you are even just a tiny bit computer savvy. I still miss being able to make folders and files (you can, with save editing, but it's not very confortable), a proper text editor, a better network map and probably too some kind of endless mode. Oh well.

Oh, and keep a look out for wild Carpenter Bruts. Otherwise he might sneak up on you and hit you with PURE UNFILTERED SWEETNESS when you least expect it.
